title: Finding functions in raw code
description:
Find likely function starts in a block of MSVC x64 machine code with no symbols, using the two kinds of evidence from lesson 2.02:

```cpp
bool looksLikePrologue(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& code, std::size_t at);
std::vector<std::size_t> findFunctions(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& code);
```

**looksLikePrologue** is true when the bytes at `at` begin with one of these (`??` is any byte), with every byte of the pattern inside the buffer:

| Pattern | Instruction |
|---|---|
| `55`, `53`, `56`, `57` | `push rbp`, `push rbx`, `push rsi`, `push rdi` |
| `40 53`, `40 55`, `40 56`, `40 57` | the same pushes with a REX prefix |
| `41 54`, `41 55`, `41 56`, `41 57` | `push r12` to `push r15` |
| `48 83 EC ??` | `sub rsp, imm8` |
| `48 81 EC ?? ?? ?? ??` | `sub rsp, imm32` |
| `48 89 ?? 24 ??` or `4C 89 ?? 24 ??` where the third byte's bits match `01 ??? 100` | saving a register at `[rsp+imm8]` |

**findFunctions** returns, in increasing order, every offset that is a **candidate** and looks like a prologue. Offset 0 is always a candidate; so is any offset whose byte is not `CC` but the byte before it is `CC` (the end of int3 padding).
hints: Write `looksLikePrologue` as a list of checks, each guarded by "are there enough bytes left?". The register-save pattern's third byte has `mod = 01` and `rm = 100`, which is `(byte & 0xC7) == 0x44`.

The last test shows the weakness of the method: a `CC` that is part of an instruction's immediate value makes the next byte look like the end of padding. Real tools combine many kinds of evidence (`.pdata`, call targets) for exactly this reason.
